en: Points of Controversy,
Great Chapter Fifteen,
Seventeenth Section.
The Discourse on the Purification of the Offering:
Is it the case that a gift is purified by the donor alone, and not by the recipient?
Yes, it is.

"Is it not the case that there are certain recipients who are worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of gifts, worthy of reverential salutation, and an unsurpassed field of merit for the world?
"Yes.

"If indeed there are certain recipients who are worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of gifts, worthy of reverential salutation, and an unsurpassed field of merit for the world, then surely, sir, you ought not to say—"
“Giving is purified by the giver alone, not by the recipient.
Is it the case that giving is purified by the giver alone, and not by the recipient?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that the Blessed One has stated that there are four pairs of persons, eight individual persons, who are worthy of offerings?
Yes, it is so.
If indeed the Blessed One has stated that there are four pairs of persons, eight individual persons, who are worthy of offerings, then certainly you should not say this: [that they are not worthy].
“Giving is purified by the giver alone, not by the recipient.
Is it the case that giving is purified by the giver alone, and not by the recipient?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that there are some who, having given a gift to a stream-enterer, fulfill the act of dedication?
Yes, they do.
If it is true that there are some who, having given a gift to a stream-enterer, fulfill the act of dedication, then indeed, sir, you should not say [that such an act is fruitless].
“Is it only from the giver that a gift is purified, and not from the recipient?
Is it not the case that there are some who are once-returners … pe … non-returners … pe …?
Is it not the case that there are some who, having given a gift to an Arahant, fulfill the act of merit?
Yes, it is so.
If indeed there are some who, having given a gift to an Arahant, fulfill the act of merit, then surely you should not say: [that there is no such thing].
“Giving is purified by the giver alone, not by the recipient.
Is it the case that giving is purified by the recipient?
Yes, it is.
"One person is the doer for another; pleasure and pain are produced by another; one person acts and another experiences [the result]"?
One should not say this... [and so forth]...
"Is it only from the giver that a gift is purified, and not from the recipient"?
“Yes.
“But was it not said by the Blessed One:
‘Ānanda, there are these four purifications of offerings’?”
Which four?
There is, Ānanda, an offering that is purified by the giver, not by the recipient;
there is, Ānanda, an offering that is purified by the recipient, not by the giver.
“There is, Ānanda, an offering that is purified both by the giver and by the recipient;
there is, Ānanda, an offering that is purified neither by the giver nor by the recipient.
These, Ānanda, are the four purifications of offerings.”
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
“Generosity is purified by the giver alone, not by the recipient.
The Discussion on the Purification of the Offering is finished.
This is the seventeenth chapter.
Its summary verse:
There is an accumulation of merit for an arahant; there is no untimely death for an arahant.
All this arises from karma;
suffering is indeed bound to the faculties;
with the exception of the Noble Path, all remaining conditioned phenomena are suffering.
The Saṅgha accepts the offering;
the Saṅgha purifies the offering;
the Saṅgha eats, drinks, chews, and tastes.
What is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit;
there is giving for the sake of purification.
